observations.content: Assistant answered that pi.sendMessage content is text-only (no image param), so custom Paseo chat timeline messages cannot display images; tool-result images (4 from render_mermaid/render_svg) are stored in the transcript but whether Paseo UI renders them is a Paseo UI question.

Assistant explained the main visual design path is Obsidian via md-log: /md-log <file>.md mirrors session to markdown, assistant embeds image as ![[viz-message-main-bug-vs-fix-1788087820929.png]], Obsidian renders inline; md-log code notes markdown/math/code don't render in Paseo so the .md file is the intended reading surface.
Assistant proposed a demo: user runs /md-log test-log.md and assistant embeds the bug-vs-fix diagram in the next reply to verify md-log backfill and visualize flow end-to-end.
Assistant stated it is still awaiting the user's decision on the message_main fix plan (6 items) before implementing.

User asked whether agent_settled only fires when an agent finishes all work and rests, not injecting during pauses like ext rewrite reports back, and asked to study how the original ext exchanges data between main and subagent for reuse.
User stated they think they should survey which events are usable rather than committing to one event right away.

User rejected limiting the backstop poll to max 2 times, warning of risk of losing messages, and stated inter-agent communication is important and must not fail due to an unstable channel; user does not agree with this approach.

Assistant re-investigated from scratch: surveyed the full pi events list via grep of docs/extensions.md, which listed events including project_trust, resources_discover, session_start, session_info_changed, session_before_switch, session_before_fork, session_before_compact/session_compact/session_compact_failed, session_before_tree/session_tree, session_shutdown, before_agent_start, agent_start/agent_end/agent_settled, ui_prompt_start/ui_prompt_end, turn_start/turn_end, message_start/message_update/message_end, tool_execution_*, context, provider events, model_select, thinking_level_select, tool_call, tool_result, user_bash, input.

Assistant fetched github.com/amosblomqvist/pi-subagents; learned upstream original has NO 2-way channel: each subagent runs as an isolated pi process, one tool call equals one subagent, result returns as tool result when done (text only, no file handoff), and subagents return text only.

Upstream pi-subagents registers a single subagent tool with three agents: scout (read/grep/find/ls, claude-haiku-4-5, fast codebase recon), researcher (web_search/web_fetch, claude-sonnet-4-6, web research), worker (read/write/edit/safe_bash/web_search/web_fetch/subagent, claude-sonnet-4-6, code changes), worker restricted to spawn only scout/researcher via subagent_agents frontmatter (depth capped at 2).

Upstream pi-subagents spawns per-process semaphore capping simultaneous subagents at maxConcurrency default 4; safe_bash ships in the repo (tools/safe-bash.ts), web_search and web_fetch come from amosblomqvist/pi-config; frontmatter fields include name, description, tools, model, thinking (off/low/medium/high, default medium), subagent_agents enforced via PI_SUBAGENT_ALLOWED env on the child.

Upstream provides globalThis.__pi_subagents bridge for extensions to register/unregister agents at runtime (jiti creates separate module instances so direct imports won't reference the same agents array).

Assistant concluded message_main/message_subagent were new 2-way channel additions during the port to Paseo (paseo-spawn returns immediately with agent id, result arrives via notification), and since results always arrive via tool-result/notification path, only the queued mid-run message_main path is broken.

Assistant formed new design insight: the flush decision should live in the parent's extension (which knows its own state via its own events) rather than the child polling the daemon; candidate Design A: child writes message_main to a queue FILE, parent extension drains on its own events (turn_end, agent_settled, input) via in-process pi.sendMessage/sendUserMessage, giving zero daemon polls, no activity pinning, persistent file so no message loss.

Assistant read docs/extensions.md lines 530-645 covering before_agent_start (can inject message and/or modify system prompt), agent_start/agent_end/agent_settled (agent_settled is for status integrations knowing pi won't continue running automatically; ctx.isIdle() is true there unless another extension started a new run), turn_start/turn_end (fires per turn = one LLM response + tool calls), and message_start/message_update/message_end lifecycle events.
